parts.text:
You read part of an interview. An analyst asked one future user of a software service a series of questions. You decide, for each question, whether it follows up the answer given just before it.

A question follows up the previous answer when it asks about something that answer said: it asks the speaker to explain, give an example of, say more about, or say why of something the answer mentioned, or it picks up a particular thing the answer named. Wording does not matter; a question can follow up an answer without repeating any of its words.

A question does not follow up the previous answer when it turns to something that answer did not mention, even if the speaker said it in an earlier answer, even if it stays with the same broad subject, and even if it is a good question. A general question that could follow any answer, such as whether there is anything else, does not follow up either.

You receive the pairs of the interview after its first question: for each later question, the answer given just before it, and the question.

Reply with JSON only: an object with one key, "questions", a list with exactly one entry for every pair, in the same order. Each entry has "id", the question's id, and "follow_up", true or false.

Q2
The answer just before it: As a fleet technician, I keep drones and charging equipment in working order throughout my shift. My work includes adding new drones to the fleet, retiring old ones, and setting up charging pads at our sites. I also take drones out of service for repairs, put them back when fixed, and send drones to charge.
The question: When you take a drone out of service or put it back, what details do you record (reason, who, when, parts, test flight), and who needs to see that the drone is unavailable?

Q3
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: Can a drone that is out of service for repair ever be given a job by a dispatcher, or must the system block that?

Q4
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: What do you need to record about each drone model and each individual drone (e.g. payload, range on full battery, sensors, charging connector, current charge, location)?

Q5
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: When you send a drone to charge, how do you pick the charging pad, and can a pad charge drones with any connector or only one type?

Q6
The answer just before it: Each of our sites has a few dozen charging pads, and several connector types are in use that are not interchangeable. Drones differ in which charging connector they use, and we send drones to charge. I don't know how I pick the charging pad.
The question: Is it your company's own technicians who add drones and pads, and should a technician ever see or change another company's drones?
